summary: Ladd Lookout, Lewis County, WA: 40-foot DNR wooden tower built 1955, abandoned 1969; footings, a pole tower and a communications building remain in photos.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower with a 14-by-14-foot cabin of a new Division of Forestry design (plywood and glass, aluminum roof)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1969 and listed as gone. Willhite's photo captions name footings, a pole tower and an old communications building

visit.trail_note: No tower remains. Willhite describes Forest Road 74 from Highway 7 about four miles south of Elbe, with the final half mile too overgrown to drive

events.note: 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower with 14x14 cabin
Abandoned by the state in 1969; both registers list it as gone

evidence.quote: A standard lookout station consisting of a forty foot tower mounted by a 14'x14' cabin on top was constructed on Ladd Mountain in Eastern Lewis County.

evidence.supports: cabin of new Division of Forestry design, plywood and glass, aluminum roof overhang
evidence.quote: The cabin is of the new design developed by the Division of Forestry, are built of plywood and glass with an aluminum roof which overhangs the building to act as a sun shade.

evidence.quote: Although there is a nearby Ladd Mountain, Ladd Lookout is several ridges to the south.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The weebly page says the lookout was constructed on Ladd Mountain; Willhite says Ladd Lookout is several ridges south of the nearby Ladd Mountain. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: all four sources repeat the 1955 build and 1969 abandonment, and no staffing, fire or owner information was found. One web search added nothing site-specific. Access level is omitted because no source names an owner or access rule. Willhite's caption 'Preserved Ladd Lookout sign' is not used because its location is not given. Willhite's access page is undated, so its road note has no date.
